pr_title: WIP: kubelet: invalidate runtime cache on container start
pr_body:
**What type of PR is this?**
/kind bug

**What this PR does / why we need it**:
If a pod's container starts and the pod is deleted all within the 2s defaultCachePeriod of the runtime cache, then the grace periods of the containers may not be honored.  This is because `GetPods()` can return a stale `runningPod` with no containers and proceed directly to `StopPodSandbox` without properly terminating the container.

Also see https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/93210#issuecomment-661244774

~~This PR allows a caller to force and update to the cache on paths that require the latest state from the runtime.~~
This PR invalidates the kubelet `runtimeCache` whenever a container start is detect so a subsequent call to `GetPods()` will get up-to-date information.

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:
xref #93210

**Special notes for your reviewer**:

**Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?**:
```release-note
NONE
```
/sig node
/priority important-soon 

I currently haven't proved that this solves the issue, hence WIP.  I'm opening this PR to do some test runs to see if the issue occurs.  In the meantime, I am trying to develop a more concise reproducer to confirm the root-cause/fix.

/cc @liggitt @derekwaynecarr

issue_context.title: MirrorPodWithGracePeriod test flaking in 5% of pull-kubernetes-node-e2e runs
issue_context.body:
These tests have flaked consistently since https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/92442 merged: https://storage.googleapis.com/k8s-gubernator/triage/index.html?pr=1&text=not%20found&test=MirrorPodWithGracePeriod

in many cases, they are the only failure in a test run:
* https://prow.k8s.io/view/gcs/kubernetes-jenkins/pr-logs/directory/pull-kubernetes-node-e2e/1284519583780179968
* https://prow.k8s.io/view/gcs/kubernetes-jenkins/pr-logs/directory/pull-kubernetes-node-e2e/1284343925561102336
* https://prow.k8s.io/view/gcs/kubernetes-jenkins/pr-logs/pull/batch/pull-kubernetes-node-e2e/1284519583780179968/

Either the functionality introduced by that PR is not reliable, or the test is faulty.

/sig node
/priority critical-urgent
/assign @tedyu @derekwaynecarr

review_comments:
talked offline... this doesn't solve the race observing a delete from configCh and oberving a ContainerStarted event from plegCh, but it does solve the issue where a container status reflected in the API (so the kubelet clearly knew the container was running) did not inform graceful deletion

My main question now is what the load impact is for a kubelet that is rapidly creating containers:

* does invalidating here cause any pathological issues for a pod with N containers (where each individual ContainerStarted event invalidates the cache and some other path calls GetPods() per-container, resulting in N cache misses.
* do we only care that GetPods() is super up-to-date in the delete case? would it make sense to use the ForceUpdateIfOlder() method in deletePod() passing in the max status.{init}containers[*].state.running.startedAt or something?

Suggestions if we keep the current approach:

1. a test exercising this would be great if it's possible
2. I'm not sure if it would be possible to move the invalidate to the point where we make the call to create the container or not

/cc @dashpole for kubelet sync loop review expertise as well

> * do we only care that GetPods() is super up-to-date in the delete case? would it make sense to use the ForceUpdateIfOlder() method in deletePod()?

a sketch of that approach is at https://github.com/liggitt/kubernetes/commits/force-delete ... that would let us keep the benefits of the runtimeCache in most cases (only rapid start/delete cases would result in cache invalidation)
I like the deletion-only approach.  The only thing I need to check is IIRC there are a few different deletion paths.  We should make sure we actually cover all deletion cases...
